ai_observations.text: Across F-001–F-008, the direct-front stance, full-body framing, open overskirt front, leggings, and boots are consistent. A recurring prompt mismatch is overskirt length: the back/side hems generally stop around mid-calf instead of reaching ankle height or slightly above the floor. Skirt fullness and front-panel shape vary noticeably: F-001 and F-005–F-006 have broader, fuller side panels; F-002–F-004 and F-007 have narrower or more sharply shaped panels. Blouse crop length and lower-edge shape also vary, though most keep the abdomen exposed and end above the belt. F-002 has an isolated extra brown band beneath the blouse, which is not specified. Head and body proportions, the jaw-to-shoulder-length bob, and equipment placement are broadly consistent; no weapons or belt equipment appear. Cross-image variation is assessable from the eight supplied images.

Across the batch, the costume and character remain broadly consistent: each image shows the teal cropped blouse, open overskirt over navy leggings, brown belt and boots, short black bob, and no belt equipment or weapons. No single image has a major structural failure.

The clearest recurring variation is the overskirt’s side-panel shape and fullness. FL-001, FL-003, FL-004, FL-005, and FL-008 have broader, fuller side drapes; FL-002 and FL-006 look narrower and straighter. In all eight, the side panels fall well below the prompt’s knee-to-upper-calf target, reaching toward the lower calf or ankle. The open center consistently reveals the leggings, but its width and the amount of fabric framing it vary. A more explicit side-hem length and panel-width target could reduce this spread.

The blouse also varies in apparent width and sleeve volume: FL-001 and FL-005 have broader, puffier sleeves, while FL-002 and FL-006 appear more compact. The short bob is consistent in length, though its silhouette varies slightly in volume and layering; there is no clear isolated hair-length defect. Body proportions and overall framing are similar, with small differences in torso angle and stance. Jewelry remains present, and no equipment-placement issue stands out.

Across FR-002–FR-008, the pointed ears are visible; FR-001 has no visible pointed ears, an isolated identity/feature discrepancy (they may be obscured by hair). The black bob stays around jaw-to-neck length across the set, with FR-001 appearing fuller and longer; this is a small recurring hair-shape variation. The body stays slim overall, though FR-001 and FR-005 read slightly broader through the torso and hips than the others. Overskirt width and fullness vary noticeably: FR-003, FR-004, and FR-006 have broad, full panels, while FR-002, FR-007, and FR-008 hang narrower and straighter; FR-001 and FR-005 are also broad, with FR-005’s front opening appearing comparatively narrow. In all candidates, the side panels fall well below the prompt’s knee-to-upper-calf target, approaching lower-calf or ankle length, so the high-low transition is subdued. Tops, belts, leggings, and boots are broadly consistent; no image shows belt equipment or weapons. The images share similar major costume structures, with no clear isolated garment-construction defect beyond FR-001’s missing visible pointed ears.

Reviewed all eight supplied LEFT_PROFILE images; no images are missing. A recurring variation is the overskirt silhouette: PL-002 and PL-005 have fuller, longer rear drapes; PL-003 and PL-004 read as more open, split panels; PL-006 has the shortest hem, ending around mid-calf with more leggings exposed; PL-008 is comparatively narrow and also ends higher. PL-001, PL-007, and the others fall between these shapes. A clearer profile template could set consistent panel fullness, opening, and hem length. Profile consistency also varies: PL-003 and PL-004 show more of the front of the torso and skirt than the stricter side views, while buckle visibility shifts across the batch. Hair remains a short dark bob throughout, with modest differences in volume and outline. Head and body proportions are broadly consistent. No weapons or belt equipment are visible in any image.

All eight images show a consistent right-facing profile, similar head/body proportions, and a short black bob ending around the nape. No weapons or other belt equipment are visible. The main recurring variation is the overskirt silhouette: PR-001, PR-003, PR-006, and PR-008 show a clearer short-front/long-rear shape, while the rear drape in PR-002, PR-003, PR-006, and PR-008 still ends around mid-to-upper calf rather than near ankle height as specified. PR-004, PR-005, and PR-007 have a more uniformly long, narrow side panel, so the open front and high-low difference are less distinct. PR-001 has the fullest, widest rear drape; PR-004, PR-005, and PR-007 are noticeably straighter and less full. The blouse, belt, boots, and jewelry remain broadly consistent in size and placement, with no notable head/body proportion or hair-form outlier.

**Recurring variation:** All eight candidates keep the back as the dominant view and show the teal cropped blouse, exposed lower back, low brown belt, leggings, and brown boots. The main mismatch with the saved prompt is skirt length: the rear hem generally stops around mid-calf, well above the requested ankle-height center-back hem. The amount of legging visible below the skirt also varies. Hair stays in a similar short bob, and no weapons or belt equipment are visible.

- **BL-001:** Rear hem ends around mid-calf, leaving the boots and lower legs exposed; the belt appears plain.
- **BL-002:** Mid-calf hem with leggings visible below; a prominent belt buckle appears at the rear-side. The face is more visible in profile than in some candidates.
- **BL-003:** Mid-calf rear hem and plain belt; otherwise close to the recurring silhouette.
- **BL-004:** Mid-calf hem with a more uneven, angled drape at the sides; plain belt.
- **BL-005:** Isolated skirt-shape variation: a pronounced side opening exposes leggings up to the upper thigh. The rear drape still falls short of the requested ankle length.
- **BL-006:** Mid-calf hem with a noticeable band of leggings showing beneath it; plain belt.
- **BL-007:** Mid-calf hem and a visible belt tab or buckle detail at the rear-side. The head is turned farther toward the viewer, revealing more face.
- **BL-008:** Mid-calf hem and plain belt; the head also shows a clear left-facing profile.

**Single-image prompt comparison — BL-003:** Its rear-facing pose and major costume pieces match the saved prompt, but its skirt hem is substantially shorter than the requested ankle-height rear drape. Cross-image variation cannot be assessed from BL-003 alone; the batch-level comparison above reflects the supplied set of eight images.

Across BR-001–BR-008, the main recurring discrepancy is the overskirt silhouette: every image shows a continuous, roughly even calf-to-lower-calf hem, rather than the requested high-low shape with shorter side panels and a continuous rear drape reaching ankle height. This leaves the leggings and most of the boots exposed. The skirts are generally moderately full, though BR-001 flares wider and has a visibly shorter hem than the others; BR-004 and BR-006 appear among the longer, narrower variants.

The cropped blouse, exposed lower back, and low hip belt are present throughout. Sleeve volume and blouse width vary modestly: BR-001 has the broadest, puffiest appearance, while BR-002 is more compact. BR-004 has a visible belt buckle; the other belts appear plain. No weapons, containers, or other belt equipment are visible.

The short black bob and slender adult proportions are broadly consistent across the set; no clear recurring head-to-body proportion issue stands out. Hair shape varies slightly between images but remains a short bob. The supplied set contains all eight mapped images, so cross-image variation can be assessed.

Across all eight supplied candidates, the main variation is the rear overskirt silhouette. B-003, B-004, B-006, B-007, and B-008 have mostly even ankle-length hems rather than the specified center-long, gradually rising rear hem; B-001 is somewhat shorter and also nearly even. B-002 and B-005 show the opposite high-low shape, with the center hem lifted to expose leggings while the sides and rear edges hang lower. The latter shape recurs in two images; the near-even hem is more common. Skirt fullness also varies: B-002 and B-005 expose substantially more leggings, while the others largely cover them.

Hair length and form vary across the batch: B-003 and B-007 have fuller, longer, shoulder-skimming bobs; B-002, B-005, and B-006 have shorter, nape-length shapes, with B-001, B-004, and B-008 between these. A clearer reference for the preserved back-view hairstyle could reduce this recurring variation.

Visible dangling earrings appear in every candidate, despite the prompt specifying no visible earrings. The rear necklace arcs are present, and no front pendant or belt-mounted equipment is apparent. Body orientation and overall outfit placement remain consistently back-facing. Since eight images were supplied, cross-image variation can be assessed.
